question.problem:
A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion with damping. The position of the particle $y(t)$ at time $t$ is governed by the equation

$$
{y}^{″}+6{y}^{′}+18y=45\operatorname{cos}⁡3t.
$$

Which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for $y(t)?$

I. $y=R{e}^{-3t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ)+4\operatorname{sin}⁡3t$

II. $y=A{e}^{-3t}+B{e}^{3t}+\operatorname{cos}⁡3t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t$

III. $y={e}^{-3t}(A\operatorname{cos}⁡3t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡3t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t$

Note that $A,$ $B,$ $R$ and $ϕ$ are constants.
question.worked_solution:
The general solution is the sum of the complementary solution and the particular solution:

$$
y(t)={y}_{c}(t)+{y}_{p}(t)
$$

First, we find the complementary solution ${y}_{c}(t),$ which is the solution to the homogeneous equation ${y}^{″}+6{y}^{′}+18y=0.$ Writing down and solving the characteristic equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+6\lambda +18 & =0 \\ ({\lambda }^{2}+6\lambda +9)-9+18 & =0 \\ (\lambda +3)^{2}+9 & =0 \\ (\lambda +3)^{2} & =-9 \\ \lambda +3 & =\pm 3\text{i} \\ \lambda  & =-3\pm 3\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore the complementary function ${y}_{c}(t)$ can be expressed in any of the following forms:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{c}(t) & =R{e}^{-3t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ), \\ {y}_{c}(t) & =R{e}^{-3t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t+ϕ), \\ {y}_{c}(t) & ={e}^{-3t}(A\operatorname{cos}⁡3t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡3t).\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(t).$ The particular solution is of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡3t+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡3t.
$$

By substituting the particular solution into the differential equation and equating coefficients, we find that $\alpha =1$ and $\beta =2.$ So, the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡3t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t.
$$

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

$$
\begin{aligned}y(t) & =R{e}^{-3t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ)+\operatorname{cos}⁡3t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t, \\ y(t) & =R{e}^{-3t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t+ϕ)+\operatorname{cos}⁡3t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t, \\ y(t) & ={e}^{-3t}(A\operatorname{cos}⁡3t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡3t+2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t.\end{aligned}
$$

Only III matches the forms above. Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".
